hypothesis: Add two aggregated-historical popularity features — a smoothed (Bayesian-shrunk) video positive-rate bucket and an author-level positive-rate bucket, both computed strictly from train-period rows only (never touching the row's own label) — as two new categorical fields in data.py. Per the EDA's popularity-skew finding (top 1% of videos drive ~24% of positives, Gini=0.79) this is high-value signal the model currently only gets indirectly through noisy per-video-id embeddings; giving it an explicit smoothed rate especially helps videos/authors with thin exposure history where the id embedding itself is undertrained.
expected_effect: nDCG@5 should improve more than GAUC, since explicit popularity signal most directly sharpens the relative top-5 ordering of candidates within a user's session, whereas GAUC (per-user pairwise ranking averaged across the whole candidate pool) is less sensitive to this global-popularity signal.
